title: Deal redline sprint notes
body:
Purpose / context:
- Sprint-style sprint: boil down negotiation levers for the customer pilot + standard enterprise attachment. Quick reference for AE and SE in calls.
- Keep this lightweight: three escalation tiers, fallbacks, and one-line suggested language for each hot clause.

Immediate negotiation goals (order of priority):
1) Limit indemnity to IP and third-party claims; avoid data-related broad indemnities.
2) Cap aggregate liability at committed fees (12 months) with carveouts for willful misconduct and gross negligence.
3) Preserve right to use model outputs and derivative models; avoid transfer of IP to customer for outputs.
4) Data residency: provide options (hosted vs private). For hosted customers insist on contractual controls, not blanket localization.

Clauses to watch and suggested tactics (compact):
- Indemnity:
  - Problem: counterparties push for broad indemnities (including data use, regulatory penalties).
  - Ask: limit to third-party IP infringement and bodily injury/property damage; explicitly exclude regulatory fines related to customer’s own data compliance.
  - Suggested redline: "Provider's indemnity limited to third-party claims of IP infringement arising from Provider-delivered software and services."
  - Escalation: legal -> commercial; fallback: mutual indemnity with narrow trigger and sublimit.

- Liability / cap:
  - Problem: customer asks for unlimited liability or very high caps.
  - Ask: aggregate cap = greater of (12 months of fees paid under the SOW OR $1M) depending on deal size. Carveouts for gross negligence/willful misconduct, and for IP indemnity.
  - Suggested redline: "Aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months, or (ii) $[X]. Carveouts: willful misconduct; IP indemnity."
  - Escalation: if customer insists on higher cap, trade for stronger SLA credits, tighter security attestations, or longer notice periods.

- Data residency / data processing:
  - Problem: customers want strict residency + purge guarantees for training data. Also some ask that Provider never use customer data for model improvement.
  - Ask: offer two tracks: Hosted (data processed in region but may transit; contractual commitments) vs Private (VPC/on‑prem). For hosted: commit to not training on customer PII without opt-in; log retention windows; deletion on reasonable notice.
  - Suggested redline: "Provider will process Customer Data in the agreed region(s). Provider will not use Customer PII to train or improve models without Customer's prior written consent."
  - Escalation: if customer requires absolute residency, suggest Dedicated or Private offering (commercial uplift).

- Data access, audit rights, and logs:
  - Problem: customers demand full debug-level logging and continuous access to raw logs.
  - Ask: provide scoped audit rights (quarterly or on notice), summarized telemetry and accessible logs for incidents; avoid continuous remote access to raw production stores.
  - Suggested redline: "Provider will provide logs and records sufficient to demonstrate compliance and investigate incidents. Audit access to raw systems will be provided subject to reasonable notice and redaction of Provider confidential information."

- Security / incident response:
  - Problem: vague timelines for breach notification and remediation.
  - Ask: 72-hour notification for confirmed incidents affecting Customer Data, 24/72/7 escalation matrix for PS/SE involvement, remediation plan within X days.
  - Suggested redline: "Provider will notify Customer of confirmed incidents affecting Customer Data within 72 hours and provide regular updates until resolved."
  - Escalation: tighten SLA remedies and require tabletop exercise for large deals.

- IP ownership and outputs:
  - Problem: customers want assignment of outputs or model improvements derived from their data. This undermines product.
  - Ask: retain ownership of models and platform. Grant customers a license to outputs for their internal business purposes. Explicitly allow Provider to use aggregated, anonymized metrics to improve service.
  - Suggested redline: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Data. Provider retains ownership of Service, Models, and model improvements. Provider grants Customer a non-exclusive license to model outputs for internal use."

- Subprocessing and flow-downs:
  - Problem: customers want full visibility + right to veto subprocessors.
  - Ask: provide current subprocessor list, 30-day notice for new subprocessors, right to object for reasonable grounds related to law/data residency; do not accept blanket veto.
  - Suggested redline: "Provider will maintain a list of subprocessors and provide 30 days' notice prior to onboarding material subprocessors. Customer may object on reasonable legal/regulatory grounds."

- SLA and service credits:
  - Problem: customers ask for punitive SLAs or excessive credits tied to downtime.
  - Ask: standard uptime SLA (e.g., 99.5% or as negotiated), clear credit schedule, cap on credits (e.g., credits not exceed fees for impacted month). Consider availability tiers for Dedicated.
  - Suggested redline: "Service availability SLA and credit schedule as set forth in Exhibit A. Credits limited to monthly fees for impacted service; credits are sole remedy for SLA failures."

- Export controls / compliance, sanctions screening:
  - Problem: customers want broad warranties re export controls, sanctions, and later try to shift risk.
  - Ask: standard warranty that Provider complies with applicable sanctions/export laws, but exclude responsibility for Customer's use that violates laws.

Negotiation playbook (talking points by persona):
- For AE/SE on discovery calls: "We have hosted and private deployment options; if residency is a hard requirement we can map to Dedicated/Private. For most customers, contractual commitments cover region + deletion."
- For commercial: "We're happy to be transparent on subprocessors and provide audit reports. For IP and outputs we need to retain model ownership to keep improving the product for everyone."
- For legal escalation: provide suggested trade-offs (higher cap <-> stronger SLA/insurance; wider data access <-> DPA/limitations).

Draft fallback language and mini playbook (short):
- If customer insists on data-use-for-training prohibition: accept for limited term (12 months) with renewal review; require fee uplift.
- If customer insists on higher liability cap: propose mutual liability and increase to 24 months fees instead of unlimited.
- If customer demands raw logs: offer redacted or filtered debug logs and a schedule for on-site review under NDA.

Open questions / to verify before next call:
- For this specific pilot, is the customer requiring formal SOC2 + penetration test before signature? (Priya to confirm)
- Any non-US residency jurisdictions? Customer mentioned Germany and Brazil — need to confirm whether Brazil data localization applies.
- Is the commercial team willing to reduce revenue credits to increase liability cap slightly?

Notes to self (tone: informal):
- Keep examples short when talking to customer — they don't want legalese up front. Use plain language: "We don't train on your PII without consent" vs "Provider will not derive model improvements from Customer Data".
- Bring up Dedicated early if questions about residency — positions upgrade instead of concession.

Reference snippets (quick copy-paste):
- Minimal liability cap clause: "Except for willful misconduct and IP indemnity, neither party's liability shall exceed fees paid in the prior 12 months."
- Data training carveout: "Provider will not use Customer Data containing PII to train Provider models without written consent."

End-of-sprint checklist (action items):
- [ ] Priya: confirm SOC2 / pentest ask and share report link (by 2025-02-06).
- [ ] Omar: produce Dedicated pricing uplift numbers + T&Cs (by 2025-02-07).
- [ ] Maya: prepare 1-page AE cheat sheet summarizing three tracks (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) by next call.

Last-minute redlines to watch during redline pass:
- Any "no cap" language, especially tied to data use or regulatory fines.
- Any clause requiring permanent transfer of IP in outputs.
- Broad audit rights granting continuous access to provider systems.
- Vague breach notification timelines or undefined remediation obligations.

---
This is intentionally terse — use as jump pad on calls. Keep a copy in the shared drive when we convert to final template.
